utility_name: Public Service Co of New Hampshire (Eversource NH)
rule_summary: Follows the NH state rules (RSA 362-A:9, En 900, Puc 900 until En 1000 takes effect). Deltas: projects >100 kW and all non-inverter projects use Eversource's Guidelines for Generator Interconnection and need a $500 non-refundable pre-application through PowerClerk. Inverters must be UL 1741 SA with ISO-NE Source Requirement Document ride-through. Eversource runs the ConnectedSolutions battery DR program in NH ($225 per average kW per season, 30-60 events, 3-8 pm, Jun-Sep). The battery must perform under its interconnection agreement.
ic_application_fee: $200 up to 25 kW, $500 for 25-100 kW, $1,000 over 100 kW, plus a $500 non-refundable pre-application for >100 kW/non-inverter. Engineering-hour charges apply above 10 kW.
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear: Eversource NH pages set no charge-source rule for batteries in net metering or ConnectedSolutions. From 2027-01-01, state law (Ch. 309) requires exporting storage to charge only from on-site NEM generation unless a third party (e.g. utility/aggregator) controls charging.
storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to an existing net-metered system: Eversource requires written notice when facility information changes (capacity increase, inverter replacement). No Eversource statement found on whether adding storage changes NEM 2.0 or legacy standard-tariff status: Unclear. The newly adopted En 1000 (DOE, adopted 2026-07-17) routes 'addition of an energy storage device' to an existing DER through the utility's modification process (En 1004.04(d)).

rule_summary: Follows NH state net-metering and interconnection rules. Delta: Liberty's utility-owned Tesla Powerwall Battery Storage pilot (DE 17-189), now closed to new applicants. Participants pay $25/battery/month x 2 for 10 years (or $4,866 upfront) and move to a 3-period TOU rate. Liberty charges the batteries off-peak and, at its monthly peak, discharges excess to the grid. That export is compensated at net-metering rates, and Liberty keeps a 20% reserve.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes (pilot only, closed to new): Liberty programs the utility-owned batteries to charge off-peak, i.e. from the grid, and credits exports at its monthly peak at net-metering rates. This is the utility-controlled-charging case that NH Ch. 309 exempts from the charge-only-from-solar rule from 2027. Customer-owned batteries: no Liberty-specific rule found, so state default (Unclear before 2027).
storage_specific_notes: The pilot uses Liberty-owned batteries. A customer-owned (BYOD) option depends on a PUC-approved working-group design that the page says is not yet available. No Liberty statement found on adding a battery to a legacy/NEM 2.0 system: Unclear.

rule_summary: Member-owned co-op, deregulated since 2000; sets its own net-metering terms in NHEC Terms & Conditions Section X and its Schedule of Rates. Renewable generation and storage facilities ('interconnection-facility') up to 1 MW AC inverter nameplate, behind the meter. Exported Energy is credited at NHEC's own per-kWh export rates, with the Co-op Power portion withheld for competitive-supply members. Dollar credits carry forward, and a check can be requested once the balance is >=$50 after the March, June or September cycle. Legacy 'Below the Cap' members bank kWh, and banks >600 kWh can be paid at the NH PUC avoided cost. Group hosts are trued up to avoided cost by June 1. Additions to an installation must be wired through the same meters.
export_credit_value: Residential N02A (eff 2026-08-01): $0.14662/kWh exported for the first 2,000 kWh, then $0.12180/kWh. Optional Net Metering Time of Day (solar or battery members only): on-peak export (M-F 4-8 pm) $0.20115/kWh, off-peak $0.11765/kWh. Delivered TOD rates: $0.49277 on-peak vs $0.19997 off-peak.
ic_application_fee: $220 up to 25 kW AC; $600 for >25-100 kW; $1,000 over 100 kW; $320 site-visit fee for each re-inspection after a failed one (Schedule of Fees eff 2026-01-01)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear: NHEC T&C Section X covers storage within 'interconnection-facility' but has no charge-source restriction. The NM TOD rate pays a higher on-peak export credit to battery members with no stated rule against grid-charged exports. Whether NH Ch. 309 (2027) binds NHEC's own tariff is not verified.
storage_specific_notes: Storage explicitly allowed under net metering (T&C X.1). Adding a battery: NHEC requires additions to run through the same meters (X.2.b). Raising AC inverter nameplate during review costs the queue position. No provision found on whether adding storage changes a member's legacy 'Below the Cap' status: Unclear. The NHEC Transactive Energy Rate pilot (50 members) pays hourly day-ahead avoided-cost prices on exports.

rule_summary: Follows VT Rule 5.100 and Rule 5.500. Deltas: GMP applies IEEE 1547-2018 (with 1547a-2020) + UL 1741 SB to all interconnection applications/registrations received after 2024-01-01. GMP states a 15-day issue-notice window for projects <=25 kW and 31 days above (Rule 5.510 sets these by export capacity at 15 kW). Storage programs: Energy Storage System Service (GMP-leased Powerwalls, $55/mo x 120 or $5,500 upfront) and Bring Your Own Device (tariff eff 2023-08-17, available until 2026-09-30). BYOD requires the customer to enable grid charging and gives GMP continuous access to dispatch for peaks and wholesale value. Incentive: $850/kW (3-hr) or $950/kW (4-hr), up to 10 kW, +$100/kW in constrained areas; self-consumption flat $850. The battery may be used only for home backup outside GMP control.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-but-not-credited: BYOD requires grid charging. Compensation is the upfront BYOD incentive, not net-metering credit, and Rule 5.137 bars NM compensation for electricity from any source other than the NM system. How GMP meters or excludes battery exports from NM credit: Unclear (GMP's solar+battery wiring requirement PDF is a drawing that did not render).
storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to an existing NM system: GMP requires its Gross Solar Meter / Battery Storage request form and checklist and has a separate solar-with-battery (DC-coupled) service requirement. Whether the addition triggers a CPG amendment or affects legacy (pre-2017) status is not stated: Unclear. BYOD sunset 2026-09-30; successor terms not found (mid-transition).

rule_summary: Municipal utility under VT Rule 5.100 and 5.500 (Commission rules apply to munis); BED Self-Generation and Net-Metering Tariff eff 2024-08-01. Deltas: excess generation is monetized at BED's own blended residential rate ($0.157506/kWh), which is lower than the statewide rate, so BED uses the lesser. Pre-existing (NM 1.x) systems get the RS tail-block rate for 10 years (plus $0.052265/kWh solar incentive for NM 1.1), then $0.157506. Non-bypassable charges: customer, energy efficiency, energy assistance, on-bill financing and equipment rental. Systems >15 kW need BED Rule 5.500 interconnection approval before CPG registration.
export_credit_value: $0.157506/kWh BED blended residential rate (tariff eff 2024-08-01) plus CPG adjustors. NM 2.6 (CPG from 2024-08-01): REC transferred $0.00 / retained -$0.04; siting Cat I -$0.04, Cat II -$0.04, Cat III -$0.07, Cat IV -$0.08. BED's 2026 biennial-update values (Cat I/II -$0.05 from 2026-08-01) are not yet in the posted tariff.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-but-not-credited: tariff §IX.K repeats Rule 5.137. Storage connected to an NM system must be configured so the customer gets no NM compensation for electricity from other sources.
storage_specific_notes: Retrofit risk: a pre-existing (pre-2017) system loses pre-existing status if amended on/after 2024-03-01 to raise capacity by more than 5% or 15 kW, whichever is greater (tariff §V.B). Adding storage alone is not listed as a capacity increase: Unclear whether BED would treat an AC-coupled battery inverter as added capacity. NM systems may not join wholesale markets without a Commission finding (§IX.J). BED runs a Moduly home battery pilot.

rule_summary: Co-op under VT Rule 5.100 and 5.500 (Commission rules apply). Credits at the statewide blended rate ($0.2071/kWh). Siting charge for applications dated 2026-08-01 or later: 5c/kWh for <=150 kW, 7c for >150 kW on a preferred site, 8c otherwise. REC-retention charge 4c/kWh. Customer charge and energy-efficiency charge are non-bypassable. Credits expire after 12 months. Deltas are VEC's own fees.
ic_application_fee: One-time account set-up charge: $33 (single or groups up to 3 accounts), $66 (4-15), $132 (>15). Second (production) meter: $160.80 plus $80 installation. Rule 5.500: $600 application fee >150 kW; $300 optional pre-application report.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-but-not-credited (state Rule 5.137 applies). VEC's Home Battery Flexible Load program pays for 4-hour peak-event dispatch: monthly credit = $6.40 x kWh x (1 - reserve) / 4, or upfront $268 x same formula plus half the monthly credit, for batteries installed from 2025-10-01 (min 10 kWh / 2 kW). The page states no charge-source rule.
storage_specific_notes: No VEC statement found on adding a battery to an existing NM system or on how battery exports are metered against NM credit: Unclear. Pre-2017 systems keep legacy compensation for 10 years from commissioning, then move to the blended rate.

rule_summary: Follows MPUC Ch. 313 / Ch. 324 and 35-A §3209-A/B. Delta: CMP's battery-storage CNEBA (Single Owner-Multiple Accounts form, Jul 2021) implements the Docket 2020-00332 advisory ruling. It requires controls that stop the paired battery charging from the grid (or, if it can grid-charge, stop it discharging to the grid). Facilities >100 kW need a yearly attestation. Battery discharge to the grid is limited to 8 am-8 pm on non-holiday weekdays (the window can shift with the ISO-NE peak). CMP may require extra metering at customer cost to track battery discharge. The NEB tariff-rate program needs a customer-paid revenue-quality meter and phone line. Pre-2019-00197 agreements get a new 20-year term when modified.
export_credit_value: Tariff rate CY2025 (Original): small commercial $0.204101, medium $0.202185, large $0.183451/kWh; Alternative: $0.139002 / $0.136406 / $0.150597 (MPUC). 2026+ values per 2025-12-17 order (not read).
grid_charging_allowed: Requires non-export: a paired NEB battery must not grid-charge, or if it can grid-charge it must not discharge to the grid. If attestation lapses or controls are removed, the agreement can be terminated immediately and credits refunded.
storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to an existing NEB system: the customer must disclose it on the Ch. 313 application/agreement and install grid-charge controls. Removing both battery and controls ends the attestation duty. Under PL 2025 c. 430, amendments after 2025-06-01 cannot extend the delivery-period end date, so a retrofit amendment does not buy extra term. CMP FAQ says pre-2019-00197 agreements get a 20-year term when modified (tension with c. 430, unresolved).

rto: ISO-NE (Bangor Hydro District); NMISA (Maine Public District)
rule_summary: Follows MPUC Ch. 313 / Ch. 324. Deltas: two districts with separate NEB tariffs and CNEBA forms. The Maine Public District is in the northern Maine (NMISA) market, not ISO-NE, and caps accounts per NEB arrangement at 10 (35-A §3209-A(3)). The NEB application asks whether storage is present and whether it is AC- or DC-coupled. The customer affirms controls so the battery is not charged from the grid, or, if grid-chargeable, does not discharge to the grid.
nem_aggregate_cap: Maine Public District: max 10 accounts/meters per NEB arrangement
grid_charging_allowed: Requires non-export (application affidavit mirrors the MPUC advisory ruling)
storage_specific_notes: Battery retrofit: disclose on the Ch. 313 NEB application (storage yes/no, AC or DC coupled) and certify grid-charge/discharge controls. No Versant-specific attestation cadence or discharge window found (unlike CMP): Unclear.
